model_interpretation.claim: A full 32-lane warp owning a 32x32 tile may improve the warp-register transpose by producing one fully coalesced 32-float store segment per instruction and avoiding multiple warps for each tile. This mapping costs five exchange stages (16 lane/register pairs per stage, 80 shuffle calls per tile) and 32 values per lane, so register pressure or shuffle cost could outweigh the mapping benefit. Grouping four independent tile-owning warps in a CTA may reduce CTA scheduling overhead without requiring shared memory or a block barrier; controller timing and build diagnostics must decide.

model_interpretation.claim: Four warps per block cover one 32×32 input tile as 8×32 strips. Each lane first owns eight row values for its input column; four 8-lane groups then transpose their 8×8 subtiles by swapping lane/register bits with warp-local XOR shuffles. This should produce coalesced input loads and contiguous 8-float store segments without shared memory or a block barrier. The extra shuffle instructions and segmented stores may offset that benefit, so candidate timing is needed.
